text:
Connor McDavid needed a point to keep his season-opening streak alive, and he made one out of almost nothing: an unassisted wrist shot at 6:42 of the first that goes in about four times in a hundred. That's 19 straight games with a point to start the season, per NHL.com. On a night when the Rangers were the better team, Edmonton needed it, and it needed Devon Levi even more.

New York had the first period, 1.40 to 0.45 on expected goals (the quality of the chances), and Levi stopped the best of it, a 38 percent look from Noah Laba. Leon Draisaitl made it 2-0 at 2:59 of the second, with Vasily Podkolzin and Mattias Ekholm assisting, pushing Edmonton's win chance from 70 to 84 percent. Jaroslav Chmelař answered at 5:05 while the Rangers were shorthanded, set up by Mika Zibanejad, in a game where he played 6:42.

The Rangers kept coming and Levi kept stopping them. They went 0 for 5 on the power play despite 1.36 expected goals with the extra man, and Levi's biggest save came late in the third on Tye Kartye. Draisaitl closed it at 18:47, an unassisted shorthanded goal on a 53 percent chance, his second of the night. Levi finished with 28 saves on 29 shots, 2.6 goals saved above expected and 0.6 wins added, the most in the game. Daily Faceoff Edmonton's verdict: "Devon Levi slams door."

By the process, this was a Rangers game. They out-attempted Edmonton 60 to 40, won expected goals 3.6 to 1.96, and won 85 percent of our replays of every shot. Adam Fox was the third star without a point, on the ice for 2.14 expected goals for in 25:24. Dylan Garand, carrying the load in a week when the Rangers put James Reimer on unconditional waivers, stopped 17 of 19. The three-game winning streak is over, and Edmonton has now beaten New York twice, after a 4-1 win on Nov. 1. The Oilers will take it. They'd be wise not to make a habit of it.
headline: Levi steals one, McDavid's streak reaches 19
